derivation: Rows: registry order (methodology.json file order); status of a module = its settled head status, else 'unrun' if the module is in the run's scope (required-edge closure of requested_modules), else 'not_in_pathway' (registry.idle_statuses). Numbered 1..N in registry order over in-scope modules (report_view.navigator); footer rows are not numbered. Glyph and word from the status table; colour from the family table, neutral grey when the registry module has no family. A rejected attempt has no row. Counts are exact integers. A link target is the module page '<id> · <title>'; only accepted and restricted heads carry output, so every other row lands on an honest status page. A not_in_pathway module inside the dependency closure of the Pathway preset reads 'Not run' (see rules.override_excluded_preset_modules).

rules.never_link_to_missing_content: Every href in the navigator and rail resolves to a page the shell draws: module routes through report.modules (all registry modules except rejected attempts), the five fixed destinations, and calculation.json only when CP-MODEL published (receipt.model.files). An unrun, blocked or not-in-pathway module links to its status page and promises no findings: has_output false, the empty-state message shown, the status word in the chip.
rules.no_journal_head: CP-OS has no attempt, head, ticket or journal entry; the store and receipt are unchanged
rules.binding: proof.receipt_content_sha256 == OwnerRunReceipt.content_hash() of the verified receipt; proof.page_sha256 == sha256 of the rendered page bytes; proof.snapshot_sha256 == receipt.snapshot_sha256. Neither hash is a literal here: both are run-time values asserted by relation.
rules.rail_limits_dot: Limitations destination reads 'with limitations' when any report module carries limitations or front.unplaced.length > 0 (app.js:680). The oracle values derive from the heads alone (a restricted or blocked head carries limitations); an unplaced binding would also light it and needs the real store.
rules.hash_links_all_resolve: Every '#' href on the rendered page resolves to a page (the shell skip link included since 0d, rule shell_skip_link): navigator and footer rows, the six rail destinations, Front Page block links (blocks[].full_analysis_route, app.js:428), the Analysis coverage table (app.js:630) and the CP-MODEL links (app.js:604, :613). A route resolves when, after app.js routeOf (overview and workbench map to front), it is a module id or alias in report.modules, or front, analysis, FIT, evidence, limitations (app.js routeOf/moduleFor/render). cases[*].block_links and cases[*].hash_links list them per case.
rules.shell_skip_link:
Resolves since 0d (41a8fdb), text-checked: every page carries Skip to analysis and
(shell.html); app.js attaches a click handler that calls preventDefault and focuses #workbench without routing, and routeOf maps the hash 'workbench' to the front route, so a page loaded at #workbench shows the Front Page. It is listed in cases[*].hash_links.shell_skip_link and is inside the dead-link refusal like every other hash link. The CP-OS rendering criterion ('visible working links') now rests on the native DOM step alone.
rules.override_excluded_preset_modules: 0d(c) (b4ae187): a module with view status not_in_pathway that is in registry.dependencies of the Pathway's preset (PATHWAY_MODULES[run.pathway], here credit_snapshot) but outside the run's requested_modules scope reads glyph 'unrun', word 'Not run' in the navigator (report_view.module_display) and in the module payload (render.py). Its navigator row stays a footer row (in_pathway false, no number: both follow the status). The navigator footer groups outside rows by word, one <details> per distinct word in row order (app.js renderNavigation): cases[*].tally.footer_groups. The module page is the unrun page: chip 'Not run', 'No validated output is available…' (the 'not part of the Pathway' message is for glyph 'na' only). Modules outside the preset closure keep 'Not in this Pathway'.
rules.hash_links_not_derivable_without_a_real_: Which Front Page blocks are populated: only a populated block carries full_analysis_route (an honest-state block, report_view.py:1712, has none) and absent table-kind blocks are hidden (app.js renderFront); block state words, whether the Model destination shows the calculation link or the fallback text, and the unplaced list. The oracle gives the superset of links the credit_snapshot Pathway can draw; the test asserts the links actually drawn are a subset of it and every one resolves. 'Full analysis' on relative-value and committee-challenge leads to a CP-3, CP-6 'Not run' status page (in the preset, not requested); what-changed to a CP-8 'Not in this Pathway' page: resolves and promises nothing, but the label overstates it (LEAD to note).
rules.report_data_extraction: The page embeds <script id="report-data" type="application/json">DATA</script> (shell.html); DATA is json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True, separators=(',',':')) with every '<' replaced by \u003c (render.py:191-193), so the first '</script>' after the opening tag ends it and json.loads of the text between is exact. No tag, no closing tag or invalid JSON: cpos_target_missing (never a bare JSONDecodeError or AttributeError). Blocks live at report-data report.blocks[], modules at modules[], rows at nav[].
rules.target_fields_inferred: target.has_output and target.limitations_panel are inferred here from status (accepted and restricted carry facts or claims; restricted and blocked carry limitations) because the oracle has no real View. The test asserts them against the real heads' module views (facts/claims/tables non-empty; limitations non-empty). A disagreement is returned to LEAD for a ruling, never edited in the oracle.
rules.limitation_calculation_json_link: The calculation.json href is relative: it resolves only when the page is opened from a directory holding the receipt's model files. A page opened elsewhere shows a link that cannot open; CP-OS proves the link is drawn from the page fact and present in receipt.model.files, not that the file is beside the page.
